Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time officially shut down, its co-founder Antonio Pinto immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and TV tracking app called Bingers, which will place greater emphasis on social features. The full report is as follows.

Bingers is now available for download

When Whip Media announced the closure of TV Time, one of its co-founders promptly announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as "a fast and beautiful watchlist paired with a fun and engaging community".

According to an exclusive report by TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering a sense of continuity for users who have long been searching for an alternative—after all, TV Time was once one of the most popular TV tracking apps in the world.

Users who saved their data through TV Time's export tool before its closure can import their library into Bingers for a seamless transition; as for users who never exported their data, or new users trying a TV tracking app for the first time, they can build their viewing records from scratch.

Bingers has significantly strengthened its community-driven features, including user profiles, reviews, show ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity matchups. Pinto told TechCrunch that these were precisely the key elements that made TV Time beloved by users over the years:

For users who simply want to keep track of the TV shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers an independent watchlist and viewing tracking function. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays a calendar of upcoming and premiere dates, and includes a countdown feature showing how many days remain until each series premieres.

Bingers is currently available for free download on the App Store, and there are no in-app purchases at present.
